title: Strumming the Right Strings for D and A Chords (Beginner Tips)
summary: In this beginner-focused micro-lesson, the instructor explains how to strum only the appropriate strings for common open chords, emphasizing that new players should aim to avoid the thickest strings on D and A chords while recognizing that early-stage mistakes are normal. For D, the recommended focus is on the thinnest four strings; accidentally striking the 5th string is discussed as acceptable, and hitting the thickest string is discouraged but not catastrophic during practice. For A, the thickest string is generally not played, though its E note is part of the chord, and the two exterior strings both produce E. The video stresses practical practice priorities—clean chord changes and a steady beat on the first count—over perfect string accuracy during early stages, and it frames the guidance as ideal considerations to bear in mind while pursuing Chord Perfect exercises and other beginners’ practice routines.
